Messages.Author: Larry Harriman
Messages.Body:
Shawn de Lioncourt >:| (sfen...@wpo.uwsuper.edu) wrote:
: Help! I am new to this game (Tried it once). Is it me or do the directions
: just suck! I play Magic the Gathering (rather Well if you ask me :) ) but I
: couldn't make head or Fangs of this one! Is there a FAQ out there that I
: could FTP or get E-mailed to me? Or would someone be patient enough to try
: to give a quick example of the first few rounds? My Big questions are About
: Bleeding, Combat, and Hunting.

OK, here goes:

Jessica goes first. She has nothing to untap, so she skips that. For
her master phase she plays short term investment. She has no minions out, so
her minion phase is really short. Then comes transfers. She puts 4 blood on
Sarah Cobbler, bringing her into the controlled region(She chuckles evily at
this point, because she knows that Sarah is my favorite Tremere). She decides
that she likes her hand, so she doesn't discard.

Then it's my turn. The only master I have is Aching beauty, but I
have no Toreador out yet, so I can't play it. During my transfer phase, I put
4 blood on Dorian Streck, and put him into play.

On Jessica's turn she takes a blood off of her investment rather than
playing a master. During her minion phase, Sarah attempts to bleed me.
Dorian could block, but seeing as how I need him around next round to play
Aching Beauty, and Sarah has superior Thaumaturgy with which to kill my vamp,
I tell Jessica that I'm not going to block. Sarah then spends one blood, and
plays conditioning(an action modifier) to bleed me for 3. I loose 3 pool.
Jessica then transfers four blood to an unknown vampire, and says that it's my
turn.

I make Dorian achingly beautiful, and then move on to my minion phase.
Dorian pays 1 blood, and attempt to use legal manipulations(an action). Since
this is an action, I have to declare it before blocking, unlike conditioning.
Not wanting me to bleed her for 3, Jessica play Wake with Evenings Freshness,
allowing Sarah to block Dorian. She still loses 1 pool for blocking
Dorian(because of Aching Beauty), but she doesn't lose the edge.

Dorian is the acting vampire, so he does thinks first. I don't play
any manuevers, and neither does she, so combat is at close range. I dodge as
my strike. Noticing my cowardly act, Jessica decides not to play the theft of
vitae she was holding. She strikes for one hand damage, which the dodge
cancels. I definitely dont press, but Jessica does with a trap.

Next round goes pretty much the same exept that I play the majesty I
just drew instead of a dodge. Combat ends before she can even think about
using her cauldron of blood.

I transfer some blood onto an expensive Tremere, and my turn is over.

Jessica untaps Sarah, gains a blood from the edge, and takes a blood
off of her investment. Since she still has the edge, she isn't in a hurry to
bleed me, and she knows she's going to bring out a vampire to block Dorian
with later this turn, Sarah decides to hunt. Sarah gains one blood from the
bank(she's back up to four). If I had blocked her, she would have entered
combat with only 3 blood, and never would have gotten the one from her hunt.
Jessica then spends three blood to bring out Muriel-Lady Thunder.

And the game continues...

Hope that helps.

Larrx...

> fine with both meths having 4 transfers right away.

Unless the official ruling has been reversed, the staggered transfers
is intended for 2-player games as well. The rulebook specifies that
staggered transfers are to be used for "multi-player games" - very
misleading, if "multi" means two!

The reasons to stagger even a 2-player game are sound. With a staggered
ramp, consider the number of total transfers spent each turn of the
game, given two players:

1 4 8 12 16 20
2 6 10 14 18

etc. Each Methuselah on his or her turn leapfrogs the other by the same
amount. In contrast, consider the number of total transfers if you don't
stagger:

4 8 12 16 20 24
4 8 12 16 20

If you stagger the 2-player game, each Methuselah on his or her turn
"leapfrogs" the other by the same amount. If you do not, the second
Methuselah is always "catching up" to the first.

papillo the obstreperous
